card.occupation: Senior Commercial Manager (chartered quantity surveyor) at a mid-sized construction contractor based in Birmingham, working on hospital and school build projects
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Business Studies and Geography at a Solihull sixth form college; BSc in Quantity Surveying at Birmingham City University (2:1); chartered member of RICS since his late twenties, which the firm paid for and he made sure they did
card.household: Lives in a four-bed detached new-build in Shirley with his wife Claire (39, part-time HR adviser for a car parts supplier) and their two children, Oliver (11) and Isla (8). No pets. Claire wanted a dog and he talked her round to 'after the kids are older'.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Acocks Green in south Birmingham. His dad was a electrician who later ran a small contracting business, and his mum worked on reception at a GP surgery. White British, no religion. He was christened but hasn't set foot in a church except for weddings and funerals. He is the first in his family to go to university and quietly likes being the one who did well. Very much a Blues fan by inheritance, though he goes less than he says he does.
card.professional_persona: Methodical and tightly organised. He runs cost reports, valuations and subcontractor final accounts, and his spreadsheets are known in the office for being immaculate. He works 50 to 55 hours most weeks and answers emails on Sunday evenings. He is calm in disputes and never raises his voice. Subcontractors find him pleasant to deal with, right up until they realise he has negotiated them down further than they meant to go. He is comfortable pushing the rules where it suits him: he claims everything he can on expenses and talks up his own part in project wins. He is very clear in his own head that he is worth more than he is paid. He is not a schmoozer and finds the client golf days a bit of a chore, but he goes because it's where the decisions get made.
card.sports_persona: Plays golf most Saturday mornings at a members' club near Solihull, off a handicap of 14, and logs his scores in an app. Supports Birmingham City and has a half-season ticket share with a mate. Runs 5k twice a week on a fixed route at 6am, mainly to keep his weight in check rather than for enjoyment. He watches the F1 and the cricket highlights.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. He'll watch whatever crime drama or Netflix series Claire puts on, and he likes a big action film. He has been to the theatre at the Hippodrome for the kids' Christmas panto and once for a musical for Claire's birthday, and he checked his phone at the interval. Music is Oasis, Kasabian and whatever's on Absolute Radio in the car. He doesn't read fiction, but he listens to business and true crime podcasts on the commute.
card.travel_persona: One big family holiday a year, booked in January with spreadsheets of prices. It's usually all-inclusive in the Canaries, Turkey or the Algarve, somewhere with a good pool and a golf course nearby. They did Florida once for the kids. He likes knowing what he's getting and doesn't see the point of 'roughing it'. He does an occasional lads' golf weekend in Portugal or Spain. He collects airline and hotel points and has been known to bring up being upgraded.
card.culinary_persona: Plain and dependable. He can do a decent barbecue and a Sunday roast, and he is particular about his steak. Weeknight tea is usually something Claire batch-cooked, or a curry from the place on Stratford Road on Fridays. He has a bacon bap from the site canteen when he's out on a project. He doesn't drink much midweek but enjoys a good red, and he likes to know what a bottle cost.
hobbies_and_interests: keeping on top of the family finances and investments (ISAs, a bit of crypto he doesn't talk about much)
car stuff, especially his leased BMW 5 Series
DIY jobs around the house, done properly with the right tools
skills: Excel to a very high level
basic electrics, picked up from his dad
card.career_goals: Wants to be Commercial Director within five years, either at his current firm or by moving to a bigger contractor if they don't make it happen. He'd like the salary, the car allowance and the title. Has privately thought about setting up his own cost consultancy in his late forties once the kids are older, mostly because the owners he deals with seem to do very nicely.
card.voice: Measured, steady, fairly low-key. Speaks at a moderate pace and doesn't waste words. He has a softened south Birmingham accent: the vowels are there ('roight' creeps in slightly, and 'like' sounds a bit flat), but it's been smoothed by years of client meetings. He uses 'er' rather than 'erm' when gathering his thoughts, and says 'sort of' now and then. He ends points with 'yeah' or 'you know'. He might say 'give it me' or 'pass it me' without noticing, and he calls a bread roll a bap. He'll say 'tea' or 'dinner' interchangeably for the evening meal. He's comfortable with silence and will just wait rather than fill it, which can come across as a bit cool. If he mishears, he says 'sorry, say that again?' He answers questions directly and doesn't elaborate unless asked.
card.typing: Tidy and efficient. Starts sentences with a capital and uses full stops, apostrophes mostly correct. Answers are short and to the point, often one line. Occasionally uses abbreviations from work like 'approx', 'etc' or 'tbc', and writes numbers as figures. No emojis. He might drop the final full stop on a very short answer.
card.with_strangers: Polite, friendly enough, a little reserved. He makes reasonable small talk but doesn't volunteer much about himself at first. He comes across as easygoing and reasonable, rarely disagrees openly and will go along with things. He's quietly sizing people up, though, and may steer conversation towards his job title, the house or the car if status comes up. He isn't rattled by awkward questions and answers them flatly, without fuss.
small_things: his golf round on Saturday and whether he broke 85
the traffic on the M42 or the A34 into town
Blues' latest result and moaning about the owners
the kids' football and swimming lessons
a new drill or pressure washer he's bought
the BMW being in for a service
booking next year's holiday early to get a deal
deeper_things: he feels he's carried the family financially and is a bit resentful that Claire went part-time
his dad's business went under when Gareth was in his twenties, and he's determined never to be in that position
he's applied for a director role twice and been passed over, and he blames office politics
he doesn't really feel very much when people around him get upset, and Claire has told him he can seem cold
he has a few thousand in crypto that he hasn't fully told Claire about
he worries less about the kids' feelings than their grades, and knows that probably isn't ideal
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at desk height, angled slightly upward, framing him from mid-chest up and slightly left of centre. Lit mostly by daylight from a window on the right of the frame plus a cool white ceiling light, so the right side of his face is brighter. He has a round face, clean-shaven with light stubble along the jaw, mid-brown short hair cut neatly with a fade at the sides and slightly thinning at the temples. He has grey-blue eyes and no glasses, and he is looking straight at the camera with a polite, closed-mouth half-smile. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip pullover over a white collared shirt, the collar just visible. Behind him is a small home office in a box room with plain light grey walls. To the left is a tall white IKEA shelving unit with lever-arch files labelled with a label maker, a printer and a framed RICS certificate. To the right, a corner of a golf bag stands against the wall. A wall calendar from a builders' merchant hangs behind his shoulder, with dates written in neat black pen.
